questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Write the role of insulin in regulating blood sugar levels in human body. Mention the disease caused due to it. (b) How is the timing and the amount of release of insulin in the blood regulated?
questions.answer: (a) Insulin promotes glucose utilisation by the body cells, thereby reducing the blood sugar level. It stimulates deposition of extra glucose as glycogen in liver and muscles. (b) The timing and amount of release of insulin is regulated by the feedback mechanism. Insulin is released by beta-cells of pancreas when there is increase of sugar level in blood. When the level of sugar decreases, negative feedback stops the secretion of insulin.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Name the part of the human excretory system where nephrons are found. Write the structure and function of nephrons.
questions.answer: Nephrons are found in Kidneys. Structure: Nephron is the basic filtration unit in the kidney. It consists of a tubule connected with a collecting duct at one end and a cup shaped Bowman's capsule at the other end. Each Bowman's capsule contains a cluster of capillaries called glomerulus. Function: Blood enters glomerulus through afferent arteriole, filtration occurs. The filtrate passes through the tubular part where useful substances like glucose, amino acids, salts and water are re-absorbed. The remaining filtrate is urine, collected by collecting duct and carried to urinary bladder.

questions.question: It is observed that the power of an eye to see nearby objects as well as far off objects diminishes with age. (i) Give reason for the above statement. (ii) Name the defect that is likely to arise in the eyes in such a condition. (iii) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the type of corrective lens used for restoring the vision of such an eye.
questions.answer: (i) The power of accommodation of the eye usually decreases with ageing due to weakening of ciliary muscles and decrease in flexibility of eye lens. (ii) The defect is Presbyopia. (iii) Presbyopia can be corrected by using a convex lens.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: How do harmful chemicals get accumulated progressively at each trophic level in a food chain?
questions.answer: Several pesticides and other chemicals are used to protect crops from diseases and pests. These chemicals are washed down into the soil or into water bodies. From the soil, these are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and from water bodies these are taken up by aquatic plants and animals. As these chemicals are not degradable, they get accumulated progressively at each trophic level.

(b) Fresh milk has a pH of 6. When it changes into curd will its pH increase or decrease? Why?
questions.answer: (a)(i) Antacid such as magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is given to neutralize excess acid in stomach. (ii) Baking soda (mild base) is used to neutralize formic acid released by honey bee sting or methanoic acid from nettle leaves. questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (i) State the role of ATP in cellular respiration. (ii) What ensures sufficient exchange of gases in plants? (iii) State the conditions on which the direction of diffusion of gases in plant depend upon.
questions.answer: (i) ATP is consumed in glycolysis to convert glucose to pyruvate. It is also produced in electron transport chain. (ii) Maximum amount of gaseous exchange occurs in plants through stomata and lenticels. Large inter-cellular spaces ensure all cells are in contact with air. (iii) The direction of diffusion depends upon environmental conditions and requirements of the plant. At night, CO2 elimination is major. During day, CO2 from respiration is used for photosynthesis and oxygen release is major.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (i) What is the internal energy reserve in plants and animals? (ii) How desert plants perform photosynthesis if their stomata remain closed during the day?
questions.answer: (i) Internal energy reserve in plants is starch and in animals it is glycogen. (ii) Desert plants take up carbon dioxide at night and prepare an intermediate which is acted upon by the energy absorbed by the chlorophyll during the day.

questions.question: Give reasons for the following: (a) Danger signals installed at airports and at the top of tall buildings are of red colour. (b) The sky appears dark to the passengers flying at very high altitudes. (c) The path of a beam of light passing through a colloidal solution is visible.
questions.answer: (a) Red colour has the longest wavelength and deviates the least, so it can be easily seen from a distance. (b) At high altitude, the atmospheric medium is rarer so scattering of light is very low. (c) This is due to scattering of light by colloidal particles (Tyndall effect).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (i) State the rule used to find the force acting on a current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. (ii) Given below are three diagrams showing entry of an electron in a magnetic field. Identify the case in which the force will be (1) maximum (2) minimum respectively. Give reason for your answer.
questions.answer: (i) Fleming's left hand rule: Stretch thumb, forefinger and middle finger of left hand mutually perpendicular. If forefinger points in direction of magnetic field and middle finger in direction of current, thumb points in direction of motion/force. (ii)(1) Maximum force when direction of motion of electron is at right angles to magnetic field. (2) Minimum force when direction of motion is along the direction of magnetic field.

questions.answer: (i) Kitchen garden is artificial because biotic and abiotic factors are modified by humans. In forests, humans do not modify biotic or abiotic factors. (ii) 1. Balance between producers and consumers: Select inter-dependable organisms to form food web. 2. Waste management: Decomposers are important for a sustainable ecosystem.

(ii) 20,000 J of energy was transferred by the producers to the organism of second trophic level. Calculate the amount of energy that will be transferred by organisms of the third trophic level to the organisms of the fourth trophic level.
questions.answer: (i) Plants â†’ Rat â†’ Snake â†’ Hawk. (ii) According to 10% law: Energy at 2nd trophic level = 20,000 J. Energy at 3rd trophic level = 10% of 20,000 = 2,000 J. Energy at 4th trophic level = 10% of 2,000 = 200 J.

In test tube 'X', add few drops of soap solution and in test tube 'Y' add a few drops of detergent solution. Shake both the test tubes for the same period. (1) In which test tube the formation of foam will be more? Why? (2) In which test tube is a curdy solid formed? Why?
questions.answer: (ii)(1) Test tube Y (detergent) will form more foam because detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium and magnesium ions in hard water. (2) Test tube X (soap) will show curdy white precipitate (scum) because soap molecules react with calcium and magnesium salts of hard water to form insoluble precipitates.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Name the parts of a bisexual flower that are not directly involved in reproduction. (b) Differentiate between self pollination and cross pollination. List any two significance of pollination. (c) What is the fate of ovules and ovary after fertilization in a flower?
questions.answer: (a) Calyx (sepals) and corolla (petals). (b) Self pollination occurs within a flower or between two flowers of the same plant, no external agent needed. Cross pollination occurs between flowers of different plants of the same species, requires external agents. Significance: (1) Helps in production of fruits and seeds. (2) Helps in transfer of characters from both parents to offspring. (c) Ovules mature to form seed and ovary grows to form fruit.

questions.question: Almost all metals combine with oxygen to form metal oxides. Metal oxides are generally basic in nature. But some metal oxides show both basic as well as acidic behaviour. Different metals show different reactivities towards oxygen. Some react vigorously while some do not react at all. (a) What happens when copper is heated in air? (Give the equation). questions.answer: (a) 2Cu + O2 â†’Î” 2CuO (black copper oxide). (b) Amphoteric oxides behave as both acidic and basic oxides. Example: Al2O3 reacts with HCl to form AlCl3 + H2O and with NaOH to form NaAlO2 + H2O. (c)(i) Na2O + H2O â†’ 2NaOH, (ii) Al2O3 + 2NaOH â†’ 2NaAlO2 + H2O. OR (c)(i) S + O2 â†’ SO2, (ii) Sulphur dioxide, (iii) Acidic, (iv) No change (dry litmus requires moisture to show colour change).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: In order to trace the inheritance of traits Mendel crossed pea plants having one contrasting character or a pair of contrasting characters. When he crossed pea plants having round and yellow seeds with pea plants having wrinkled and green seeds, he observed that no plants with wrinkled and green seeds were obtained in the F1 generation. When the F1 generation pea plants were cross-bred by self-pollination, the F2 generation had seeds with different combinations of shape and colour also. (a) Write any two pairs of contrasting characteristics of pea plant used by Mendel other than those mentioned. (b) Differentiate between dominant and recessive traits. (c) State the ratio of the combinations observed in the seeds of F2 generation. What do you interpret from this result?
questions.answer: (a) Purple flower vs white flower, Tall plant vs short plant. (b) Dominant traits mask recessive traits and express in both homozygous and heterozygous conditions. Recessive traits express only in homozygous condition. (c) Phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1. This shows independent assortment - the inheritance of one pair of contrasting traits does not affect the inheritance of another pair. (OR) When pure violet (VV) crossed with white (vv): F1 all violet (Vv). F2 ratio: 3 violet : 1 white, genotypic ratio 1:2:1.

questions.question: State one role of each of the following in human digestive system: (a) Hydrochloric acid (b) Villi (c) Anal Sphincter (d) Lipase

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: How is the movement of leaves of a sensitive plant different from the downward movement of the roots?
questions.answer: The movement of leaves in sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica) occurs in response to touch (nastic movement), does not depend on direction of stimulus, and happens due to changes in water content, not growth. The downward movement of roots is tropic movement (geotropism), occurs in response to direction of gravity, and involves growth of root cells.

questions.question: There is a hormone which regulates carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism in our body. Name the hormone and the gland which secretes it. Why is it important for us to have iodised salt in our diet?
questions.answer: The hormone is thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland. Iodised salt is important because iodine is required for the synthesis of thyroxine; its deficiency can lead to goitre.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Show how you would connect three resistors each of resistance 6 Î©, so that the combination has a resistance of 9 Î©. Also justify your answer.
questions.answer: Connect two 6 Î© resistors in parallel: 1/Rp = 1/6 + 1/6 = 2/6, Rp = 3 Î©. Then connect the third 6 Î© resistor in series with this combination: Rnet = 3 + 6 = 9 Î©. Justification: Parallel combination reduces resistance to 3 Î©, then adding a series resistor of 6 Î© gives total 9 Î©.

questions.question: (a) Two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other. Why? (b) How is a uniform magnetic field in a given region represented? Draw a diagram in support of your answer.
questions.answer: (a) Magnetic field lines do not intersect because at the point of intersection the magnetic field would have two different directions, which is impossible. (b) A uniform magnetic field is represented by parallel, equally spaced straight lines.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) The pH of a sample of tomato juice is 4.6. How is this juice likely to be in taste? Give reason. (b) How do we differentiate between a strong acid and a weak base in terms of ion-formation in aqueous solutions? (c) The acid rain can make the survival of aquatic animals difficult. How?
questions.answer: (a) Tomato juice is sour in taste because pH 4.6 is acidic, containing natural acids like citric and ascorbic acid. (b) Strong acid completely ionises in water producing large number of H+ ions (e.g., HCl â†’ H+ + Cl-). Weak base partially ionises producing small number of OH- ions (e.g., NH4OH â‡Œ NH4+ + OH-). (c) Acid rain lowers pH of water bodies, making them acidic. Aquatic animals cannot survive as it damages gills, skin, eggs and disturbs enzyme activity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Why is respiratory pigment needed in multicellular organisms with large body size? (b) Give reasons: 1. Rings of cartilage are present in the throat. 2. Lungs always contain a residual volume of air. 3. The diaphragm flattens and ribs are lifted up when we breathe in. 4. Walls of alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessels.
questions.answer: (a) In large multicellular organisms, simple diffusion is not enough. Respiratory pigment like haemoglobin picks up oxygen in lungs, carries it through blood to body tissues, and helps transport CO2 back to lungs. (b) 1. Cartilage rings keep trachea open and prevent collapse. 2. Residual volume allows continuous gas exchange between breaths and prevents lung collapse. 3. This increases chest cavity volume, reduces air pressure, allowing air to rush in. 4. Extensive network provides large surface area for efficient gas exchange.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Define reflex action. With the help of a flow chart show the path of a reflex action such as sneezing.
questions.answer: Reflex action is an automatic, quick and involuntary response to a stimulus that does not involve the conscious part of the brain. Reflex arc: Stimulus (e.g., dust in nose) â†’ Sensory receptor â†’ Sensory neuron â†’ Spinal cord (relay neuron) â†’ Motor neuron â†’ Effector (muscles of chest and diaphragm contract) â†’ Response (sneezing to expel irritant).

questions.question: Study the diagram given below and answer the questions that follow: (a) Name the defect of vision represented in the diagram. Give reason for your answer. (b) List two causes of this defect. (c) With the help of a diagram show how this defect of vision is corrected.
questions.answer: (a) Hypermetropia (long-sightedness). Light rays from a near object converge to form image behind retina instead of on it. (b) Causes: 1. Eyeball is too short. 2. Focal length of eye lens is too long (lens less convex). (c) Corrected by using convex (converging) lens which converges incoming light before it enters the eye so image forms on retina.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Name and state the rule to determine the direction of a: (a) magnetic field produced around a current carrying straight conductor. (b) force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
questions.answer: (a) Right-Hand Thumb Rule: Hold the current-carrying conductor in right hand with thumb pointing in direction of current; curl of fingers gives direction of magnetic field lines. (b) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Stretch thumb, forefinger and middle finger of left hand mutually perpendicular. Forefinger points in direction of magnetic field, middle finger in direction of current, thumb points in direction of force/motion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Plants â†’ Deer â†’ Lion. In the given food chain, what will be the impact of removing all the organisms of second trophic level on the first and third trophic level? Will the impact be the same for the organisms of the third trophic level in the above food chain if they were present in a food web? Justify.
questions.answer: If all deer (2nd trophic level) are removed: Plants (1st) population will increase as no herbivores graze. Lions (3rd) population will decrease and may die out as food source is gone. In a food web, the impact on lions would be less severe because they have alternate prey options (e.g., zebra or goat), so loss of one prey species does not immediately threaten survival.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A gas 'X' which is a deadly poison is found at the higher levels of atmosphere and performs an essential function. Name the gas and write the function performed by this gas in the atmosphere. Which chemical is linked to the decrease in the level of this gas? What measures have been taken by an international organization to check the depletion of the layer containing this gas?
questions.answer: Gas X is ozone (O3). It forms the ozone layer in stratosphere which absorbs harmful UV radiation from the Sun, protecting living organisms from genetic damage and skin cancer. CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) are the main chemicals responsible for ozone depletion. The Montreal Protocol (1987) was signed to phase out production and use of CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Define a homologous series of carbon compounds. (b) Why is the melting and boiling points of C4H8 higher than that of C3H6 or C2H4? (c) Why do we NOT see any gradation in chemical properties of a homologous series compounds? (d) Write the name and structures of (i) aldehyde and (ii) ketone with molecular form C3H6O.
questions.answer: (a) Homologous series is a group of organic compounds with same functional group, similar chemical properties and constant difference of CH2 (14 amu) between successive members. (b) As carbon chain length increases, molecular mass and surface area increase, leading to stronger van der Waals forces, so more heat needed to separate molecules. (c) Chemical properties are determined by functional group which is same for all members, so they undergo similar reactions. (d) (i) Propanal: CH3-CH2-CHO, (ii) Propanone (acetone): CH3-CO-CH3.

questions.answer: (a) X = Ethanol, C2H5OH, structural formula: CH3-CH2-OH. (b) Dehydration of ethanol to ethene: C2H5OH â†’conc. H2SO4, 443K C2H4 + H2O. Conc. questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Name three techniques/devices used by human females to avoid pregnancy. Mention the side effects caused by each. (b) What will happen if in a human female (1) fertilisation takes place, (2) an egg is not fertilised?
questions.answer: (a) 1. Oral contraceptive pills: prevent ovulation; side effects - nausea, weight gain, mood changes, irregular menstrual cycles. 2. Copper-T: prevents implantation; side effects - abdominal pain, excessive bleeding, infection risk. 3. Tubectomy: cutting and tying fallopian tubes; side effects - pain, infection risk, permanent. (b) 1. If fertilised, zygote forms in oviduct, undergoes cell division, implants in uterus, develops into embryo/foetus (pregnancy). 2. If not fertilised, unfertilised egg and thickened uterine lining are shed as menstrual bleeding (menstruation).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Draw a diagram showing spore formation in Rhizopus and label the (i) reproductive and (ii) non-reproductive parts. Why does Rhizopus not multiply on a dry slice of bread? (b) Name and explain the process by which reproduction takes place in Hydra.
questions.answer: (a) Reproductive part: Sporangium (produces spores). Non-reproductive parts: Hyphae and Rhizoids (absorb nutrients and anchor). Rhizopus does not multiply on dry bread because moisture is essential for spore germination. (b) Hydra reproduces by budding: a small bud develops on body wall due to repeated cell division, grows into a small hydra, and detaches when mature to live independently.

questions.answer: (a) Electric power is rate at which electrical energy is consumed. P = VI. Using Ohm's law: P = IÂ²R = VÂ²/R. (b) (1) 1 unit = 1 kWh, Energy = 11 kWh, Time = 5 h, P = 11/5 = 2.2 kW = 2200 W. (2) I = P/V = 2200/220 = 10 A. (3) R = V/I = 220/10 = 22 Î©.

questions.answer: (a) Cathode: Thin strip of pure copper. Anode: Thick plate of impure copper. (b) Acidified copper sulphate solution (CuSO4). (c) At anode: Cu (impure) â†’ CuÂ²âº + 2eâ». At cathode: CuÂ²âº + 2eâ» â†’ Cu (pure). Impurities settle as anode mud. OR (c) Beaker A (Zn strip): Zn displaces Cu from CuSO4, reddish-brown copper deposit on zinc, blue colour fades. questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. (a) When Mendel crossed pea plants with pure tall and pure short characteristics to produce F1 progeny, which two observations were made by him in F1 plants? (b) Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait. (c) In a cross with two pairs of contrasting characters RRYY (Round Yellow) Ã— rryy (Wrinkled Green), Mendel observed 4 types of combinations in F2 generation. By which method did he obtain F2 generation? Write the ratio of the parental combinations obtained and what conclusions were drawn from this experiment?
questions.answer: (a) 1. All F1 plants were tall (tall dominates short). 2. The short trait reappeared in F2 showing it was not lost but only masked. (b) Dominant trait expressed in F1 even with one allele; recessive expressed only when both alleles are same (homozygous). (c) F2 obtained by self-pollinating F1 hybrids (RrYy Ã— RrYy). Phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1. Conclusion: Law of Independent Assortment - inheritance of one trait does not affect inheritance of another.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Write the molecular formula of: (i) Methane (ii) Propane. (b) Why do carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points?
questions.answer: (a) Methane - CH4, Propane - C3H8. (b) Carbon compounds are covalent compounds with weak intermolecular forces (van der Waals forces), so less energy is needed to overcome them, resulting in low melting and boiling points.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The electrons in atoms of two elements X and Y are distributed in three shells having 1 and 7 electrons respectively in their outermost shells. (a) Write their group numbers. (b) Write the molecular formula of the compound formed when X and Y combine. (c) Which is electropositive?
questions.answer: (a) X (1 valence electron) - Group 1; Y (7 valence electrons) - Group 17. (b) XY - X donates 1 electron to Y, both attain stable octet configuration. (c) X is electropositive as it donates its electron.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Which flowers have higher possibility of self-pollination among Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus? (b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower.
questions.answer: (a) Mustard and Hibiscus have higher possibility of self-pollination as they are bisexual flowers. Papaya and Watermelon are unisexual and cross-pollinated. (b) Androecium (male - stamens) and Gynoecium (female - pistil).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which one of Spirogyra and Planaria reproduces by regeneration and why? Give another example of an organism that reproduces by the same process.
questions.answer: Planaria reproduces by regeneration because it has specialised cells that proliferate and differentiate into various cell types to form complete organisms. Hydra also reproduces by regeneration.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) What is variation? List two main reasons that lead to variation in a population. (b)(i) In a cross between violet and white flowered plants, state the characteristics of F1 progeny. (ii) What is observed in F2 progeny after self-pollination of F1? (iii) If 100 plants are produced in F2, how many will show the recessive trait?
questions.answer: (a) Variation: small differences among individuals of same species. Reasons: (1) Errors in DNA copying mechanism. (2) Sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents. (b)(i) All F1 have purple flowers (dominant), genotype Vv. (ii) F2 has purple and white flowers in ratio 3:1. (iii) 25 plants show recessive white trait.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a)(i) Name and state the rule to find force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. (ii) An alpha particle is projected towards north in a magnetic field. Which direction will an electron take in the same field? (b)(i) What is a solenoid? (ii) Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines of a current-carrying solenoid.
questions.answer: (a)(i) Fleming's left hand rule: Stretch thumb, forefinger and middle finger of left hand mutually perpendicular. Forefinger - magnetic field, middle finger - current, thumb - force/motion. (ii) Electron will project towards south (opposite to alpha particle as it is negatively charged). (b)(i) A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped in a cylindrical shape. (ii) Inside solenoid: parallel, uniform field lines. Outside: similar to bar magnet.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) What is ozone? How is it formed in upper atmosphere? How does it affect our ecosystem? (b)(i) List two human-made ecosystems. (ii) Why don't we clean a pond the same way as an aquarium?
questions.answer: (a) Ozone (O3) is formed when UV radiation splits O2 into O atoms, which combine with O2 to form O3. It shields Earth from harmful UV radiation, protecting from skin cancer, cataracts, and ecosystem damage. (b)(i) Agricultural fields and aquariums. (ii) A pond is a natural self-sustaining ecosystem with decomposers that clean it. An aquarium is artificial, not self-sustaining, requiring manual cleaning to remove waste toxins.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) List two advantages of using atomic number as the basis for classification in the Modern Periodic Table. (b) Write electronic configurations of element X (atomic number 13) and Y (atomic number 20).
questions.answer: (a) Advantages: (1) Elements in same group have same number of valence electrons, correlating position with electronic configuration. (2) Completion of each period is logical - energy shells are gradually filled until inert gas configuration. (b) X(13) = 2, 8, 3. Y(20) = 2, 8, 8, 2.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Draw two possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms. What are these called? Write molecular formula and common name. Write formula of its alkyne. (b)(i) Write molecular formula and structure of benzene. (ii) How many single and double bonds in benzene? (iii) Which compounds are called alkynes?
questions.answer: (a) n-butane (CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3) and isobutane (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3). These are isomers. Molecular formula: C4H10, Common name: Butane. Alkyne: C4H6 (Butyne). (b)(i) Benzene: C6H6, hexagonal ring with alternating double bonds. (ii) 9 single bonds, 3 double bonds. (iii) Alkynes: hydrocarbons with one or more triple bonds, general formula CnH2n-2.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Give one function each of: Testis, Scrotum, Vas deferens, Prostate gland. (b) Name the germ cell that: (i) is motile (ii) stores food.
questions.answer: (a) Testis: Produces sperms (male gamete). Scrotum: Maintains 2-3Â°C lower temperature for sperm maturation. Vas deferens: Transports sperm from epididymis to ejaculatory duct. Prostate gland: Secretes alkaline fluid to neutralize vaginal acidity. (b)(i) Sperm is motile. (ii) Ovum stores food.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Three resistors R1, R2, R3 are connected in parallel to a battery, ammeter, voltmeter and key. Draw a circuit diagram. (b) Calculate equivalent resistance of network: R1=5Î©, R2=10Î©, R3=10Î©, R4=5Î© (R2,R3 parallel, then series with R1,R4).
questions.answer: (a) Circuit diagram: Battery connected through key to parallel combination of R1, R2, R3. Ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel across combination. (b) R2||R3: 1/Rp = 1/10 + 1/10 = 2/10, Rp = 5Î©. R1 + Rp + R4 = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15Î©. Equivalent resistance = 15Î©.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a)(i) Define electric power and write SI unit. (ii) Two bulbs 100W,220V and 60W,220V are connected in parallel to 220V mains. Find current drawn. (b)(i) State Joule's law of heating with mathematical expression. (ii) A 5Î© resistor connected to 6V battery. Find heat dissipated in 10s.
questions.answer: (a)(i) Electric power: rate at which electric energy is consumed. SI unit: watt (W). (ii) R1 = 220Â²/100 = 484Î©, I1 = 220/484 = 0.454A. R2 = 220Â²/60 = 806.6Î©, I2 = 220/806.6 = 0.272A. Total current = 0.727A. (b)(i) H = IÂ²Rt. (ii) I = 6/5 = 1.2A. H = 1.2Â² Ã— 5 Ã— 10 = 72J.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: (a) Which organisms form the first trophic level? Why are they called so? (b) Why are humans most adversely affected by biomagnification? (c) State one ill-effect of absence of decomposers in an ecosystem.
questions.answer: (a) Producers (plants) form the first trophic level. They are called producers because they convert light energy into chemical energy through photosynthesis, providing energy for all other trophic levels. (b) Humans are at the top of food chains, so the maximum concentration of non-biodegradable toxins accumulates in their bodies through biomagnification. (c) Without decomposers, dead organic matter accumulates, nutrients are not recycled, soil fertility declines, and the ecosystem becomes unsustainable.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: The mechanism by which sex of an individual is determined is called sex-determination. In humans, there are 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes - 44 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes (X and Y). At fertilisation, the type of male gamete fusing with the female gamete decides the child's sex. (a) Why is the pair of sex chromosomes in males called a mismatched pair? (b) Which parent has a perfect pair of sex chromosomes? Will the gametes produced be of same kind or different? (c)(i) Name two animals whose sex is not genetically determined. Explain their sex determination. OR (ii) With a flowchart, show how sex is genetically determined in humans.
questions.answer: (a) In males, one sex chromosome is normal-sized X and the other is short Y, making them mismatched (heteromorphic). (b) Female has perfect pair (XX). All eggs carry X chromosome (same kind). (c)(i) Green sea turtle: temperature-dependent - cooler (~29Â°C) produces males, warmer (~33Â°C) produces females. Snail: individuals change sex - born male, later become female. OR (c)(ii) Female (XX) produces X eggs. Male (XY) produces X and Y sperms. X egg + X sperm = XX (female). X egg + Y sperm = XY (male).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: A student sprinkles iron filings around a bar magnet on a white paper. On tapping, the filings arrange in a pattern. (a) Describe the pattern of iron filings. (b) Draw magnetic field lines of a bar magnet showing poles and direction. (c)(i) How is the direction of magnetic field determined using field lines? Why don't two field lines intersect? OR (c)(ii) How are field lines drawn using a compass needle? Draw one line on each side.
questions.answer: (a) Iron filings arrange in curved lines from north to south pole outside the magnet. Concentration is highest at poles, indicating strongest field. (b) Field lines emerge from north pole, curve through space, enter south pole. Inside magnet, lines go from south to north. (c)(i) Place a compass needle - north pole points in direction of field. Two lines never intersect because this would give two field directions at one point, which is impossible. OR (c)(ii) Place compass near north pole, mark needle ends. Move compass so south pole is at previous north mark. Repeat to trace one line. Repeat on other side. Join marked points with smooth curves.
